units.text: INT. HUSBAND - CONTINUOUS
I sincerely hope not, father. However, I am delighted at what you tell me about Robert, thoroughly delighted. It shows he has got pluck.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: He has got more than pluck, sir, he has got genius.
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: Ah! I prefer pluck. It is not so common, nowadays, as genius is.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: I wish you would go into Parliament.
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: My dear father, only people who look dull ever get into the House of Commons, and only people who are dull ever succeed there.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Why don’t you try to do something useful in life?
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: I am far too young.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Testily .
I hate this affectation of youth, sir. It is a great deal too prevalent nowadays.
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: Youth isn’t an affectation. Youth is an art.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Why don’t you propose to that pretty Miss Chiltern?
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: I am of a very nervous disposition, especially in the morning.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: I don’t suppose there is the smallest chance of her accepting you.
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: I don’t know how the betting stands to-day.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: If she did accept you she would be the prettiest fool in England.
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: That is just what I should like to marry. A thoroughly sensible wife would reduce me to a condition of absolute idiocy in less than six months.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: You don’t deserve her, sir.
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: My dear father, if we men married the women we deserved, we should have a very bad time of it.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Enter MABEL CHILTERN.
Oh! . . . How do you do, Lord Caversham? I hope Lady Caversham is quite well?
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: Lady Caversham is as usual, as usual.
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: Good morning, Miss Mabel!
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Taking no notice at all of LORD GORING, and addressing herself exclusively to LORD CAVERSHAM.
And Lady Caversham’s bonnets . . . are they at all better?
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: They have had a serious relapse, I am sorry to say.
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: Good morning, Miss Mabel!
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: To LORD CAVERSHAM.
I hope an operation will not be necessary.
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: Smiling at her pertness .
If it is, we shall have to give Lady Caversham a narcotic. Otherwise she would never consent to have a feather touched.
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: With increased emphasis .
Good morning, Miss Mabel!
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Turning round with feigned surprise .
Oh, are you here? Of course you understand that after your breaking your appointment I am never going to speak to you again.
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: Oh, please don’t say such a thing. You are the one person in London I really like to have to listen to me.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Lord Goring, I never believe a single word that either you or I say to each other.
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: You are quite right, my dear, quite right . . . as far as he is concerned, I mean.
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: Do you think you could possibly make your son behave a little better occasionally? Just as a change.
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: I regret to say, Miss Chiltern, that I have no influence at all over my son. I wish I had. If I had, I know what I would make him do.
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: I am afraid that he has one of those terribly weak natures that are not susceptible to influence.
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: He is very heartless, very heartless.
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: It seems to me that I am a little in the way here.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: It is very good for you to be in the way, and to know what people say of you behind your back.
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: I don’t at all like knowing what people say of me behind my back. It makes me far too conceited.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: After that, my dear, I really must bid you good morning.
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM
